title: Catalyst
content: Catalyst is a substance that alters the rate of a chemical reaction but remains chemically unchanged at the end of the reaction.

title: Positive catalyst
content: Positive catalyst is a catalyst that increases the rate of a chemical reaction.

title: Negative catalyst
content: Negative catalyst is a catalyst that decreases the rate of a chemical reaction.

title: Phase
content: Phase is a portion of a physical state (solid, liquid, gas) that is homogeneous throughout, and can be separated physically from other phases.

title: Homogeneous catalyst
content: Homogeneous catalyst is a catalyst which is in the same phase as the reactants in a catalyzed reaction.

title: Heterogeneous catalyst
content: Heterogeneous catalyst is a catalyst which is in a different phase from the reactants in a catalysed reaction.

title: Enzymes
content: Enzymes are proteins that act as catalysts for specific biochemical reactions.

title: Photochemical reaction
content: Photochemical reaction is a chemical reaction initiated by the absorption of energy in the form of light, resulting in specific products.

title: Activation energy
content: Activation energy is the minimum amount of energy that reacting particles must have to form the activated complex and lead to a reaction.

title: Transition state
content: Transition state (also known as an intermediate state) is a highly energetic state that would be highly unstable.

title: Collision theory
content: Collision theory states that a chemical reaction only takes place when two reacting molecules collide in the correct orientation with sufficient kinetic energy.

title: Successful collision
content: Successful collision is a collision that causes a chemical reaction.

title: Activated complex
content: Activated complex is a temporary unstable arrangement of atoms that may form products or break apart to reform the reactants.
